sourcedFrom: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. (UNDATED — nothing in the document states one)
cleanIntro:
The Sabre 10 and Sabre 15 are Palmetto State Armory's AR-pattern rifles. They come apart like any AR: the rear takedown pin, the upper pivoting open on the front pin, then the bolt carrier group and charging handle out of the back of the upper.

PSA's family book prints one set of instructions for both rifles and says the disassembly is the same for each. This guide follows it as printed.

Two things carry through: the chamber is left dry, and the cam pin must be back in the bolt group before the rifle is fired — PSA warns it can still fire without it and may blow up.

steps.title: Selector on SAFE
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, and put the safety selector on SAFE before anything else.
steps.prose: Everything after this assumes the rifle cannot fire while you work the controls.
steps.quote: Place the safety selector on SAFE
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Unloading The Firearm, printed p.18

steps.title: Magazine out — press the release, pull DOWN
steps.action: Hold the grip with your finger off the trigger, press the magazine release button and pull the magazine down out of the well.
steps.prose: The magazine comes out before the charging handle moves, so nothing new can feed.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button and pull the magazine down to remove.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Unloading The Firearm, printed p.18

steps.title: Charging handle back, press the LOWER half of the bolt catch
steps.action: Unlock the charging handle and pull it all the way back, press in on the lower part of the bolt catch, then let the charging handle go. The bolt stays locked open.
steps.prose: It is the lower half of the catch that holds the bolt open.
steps.quote: Unlock and pull the charging handle all the way out [figure 3] and press in on the lower portion of the bolt catch [figure 4].
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Unloading The Firearm, printed p.19

steps.title: LOOK into the chamber
steps.action: With the bolt held open, look through the ejection port into the chamber and confirm it is empty.
steps.prose: Seeing an empty chamber is the check. Working the action is not.
steps.quote: Look into the receiver through the ejection port and verify that there are no cartridges in the chamber [figure 5].
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Unloading The Firearm, printed p.19

steps.title: Eye protection on
steps.action: Put on eye protection before the takedown pin moves.
steps.prose: PSA asks for eye protection every time the rifle is handled for cleaning.
steps.quote: Always wear eye protection every time before handling your firearm for cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Rear takedown pin — push from the LEFT
steps.action: Push in the takedown pin from the left side of the receiver. It sits above and behind the safety lever.
steps.prose: This is the rear pin. The front pin stays where it is.
steps.quote: Push in the takedown pin, located above and to the rear of the safety lever on the left hand side of the receiver [figure 15].
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Pull it from the right until it stops
steps.action: Pull the takedown pin out from the right side of the receiver until it stops. It is captive and will not come out.
steps.prose: Stop when it stops. Do not lever it looking for a loose pin.
steps.quote: You may then pull the pin from the right side of the receiver until it stops (it will not pull out)
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Upper pivots open on the front pin
steps.action: Hold the rear of the upper receiver and lift it, letting it pivot on the front pin. The lower's fire control group is now exposed.
steps.prose: Leave the fire control group alone — PSA publishes nothing for it.
steps.quote: Grasp the rear of the upper receiver and pull up, allowing it to pivot on the front pin. This will expose the fire control group.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Bolt carrier group straight back and out
steps.action: Pull the bolt carrier straight back out of the upper until it comes free of the charging handle and the upper receiver.
steps.prose: Catch it as it comes out; do not let it drop onto the bench.
steps.quote: Pull the bolt carrier straight back until it is free of the charging handle and upper.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Charging handle back, drop it, out the rear
steps.action: Pull the charging handle back until it stops, let it drop down clear of the upper receiver, and take it out of the rear.
steps.prose: It only comes out once it has dropped down at the end of its travel.
steps.quote: Pull the charging handle back until it stops, then allow it to drop down to clear the upper receiver and remove it from the rear.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — DISASSEMBLY, printed p.25

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the upper and lower, still joined at the front pin; the bolt carrier group; and the charging handle. PSA's cleaning section has you take the bolt carrier group apart for cleaning. That, and taking the buffer and spring out of the buffer tube, is in DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Nothing else comes off for routine cleaning.
steps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — MAINTENANCE, printed p.30

deepSteps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out, firing pin out the back
deepSteps.action: Push the bolt into the carrier until it stops. Pull out the firing pin retaining pin, then slide the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier.
deepSteps.prose: Work over the bench. The retaining pin is small.
deepSteps.quote: Remove firing pin retaining pin (E) and slide firing pin (F) to the rear of the carrier until it is free.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Cam pin: quarter turn, pull straight out
deepSteps.action: Turn the cam pin a quarter turn so its head clears the gas key, then pull it straight out.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the cam pin with the bolt. It has to go back in.
deepSteps.quote: the pin to clear the gas key, and pull straight out.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the carrier
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt assembly out of the carrier assembly.
deepSteps.prose: Clean the bolt and carrier separately from here.
deepSteps.quote: The bolt assembly may now be removed from the carrier assembly.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Extractor pin out, extractor off
deepSteps.action: Push the extractor pin out and take the extractor off the bolt.
deepSteps.prose: Small parts come with it — see the next step before you lose track of them.
deepSteps.quote: Push extractor pin out to remove extractor.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Check the extractor spring and spacer
deepSteps.action: Note where the spring and spacer sit on the extractor and what shape they are in. Replace anything missing or worn.
deepSteps.prose: They go back exactly where they came from.
deepSteps.quote: Note position and condition of spring and spacer on the extractor. If items are missing or worn, replace.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: This is where PSA stops on the bolt
deepSteps.action: The bolt group is apart. PSA's book goes no further for routine maintenance — the rest of the bolt stays as it is.
deepSteps.prose: Anything past this point is for a gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No Further disassembly is required for routine maintenance.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Bolt Carrier Group Disassembly, printed p.27

deepSteps.title: Buffer tube: the spring is under load
deepSteps.action: With the upper and lower separated, the buffer and buffer spring are visible in the buffer tube. The spring is compressed — keep eye protection on.
deepSteps.prose: Keep your face out of line with the tube.
deepSteps.quote: Action spring is under compression. Please wear eye protection when removing the buffer and buffer spring.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Buffer Tube Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Hold the buffer, press the retainer pin DOWN
deepSteps.action: Hold the buffer back with one hand and push down on the buffer retainer pin.
deepSteps.prose: Do not let go of the buffer when the retainer clears it.
deepSteps.quote: Push down on the buffer retainer pin [Figure 24] while holding the buffer back.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Buffer Tube Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Ease the buffer forward, then out
deepSteps.action: Let the buffer travel forward slowly once it has cleared the retaining pin. When the spring is no longer compressed, take the buffer and buffer spring out of the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Slowly is the instruction — a released spring under control, not a launched one.
deepSteps.quote: Allow buffer to travel forward slowly after clearing the retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — Buffer Tube Disassembly, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: The cam pin goes back in
deepSteps.action: When the bolt group goes back together, the cam pin must be in it before the rifle is fired.
deepSteps.prose: ⛔ PSA warns the rifle can still fire without the cam pin and may explode.
deepSteps.quote: Be sure the cam pin is installed in the bolt group. If it is not installed, your firearm can still fire and may explode causing injury or death.
deepSteps.cite: SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL — SABRE AR FAMILY MANUAL (title on the cover, printed p.1, and the back cover, printed p.36). No date, revision or part code is printed in the book. — GENERAL TIPS AND WARNINGS, printed p.9

cleaning.name: CHAMBER
tasks: Chamber brush with bore solvent or CLP, several passes to scrub the inside of the chamber.
Wipe with clean patches until a patch stays clean.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Patch soaked in bore cleaner through the barrel several times, starting from the chamber end.
Cleaning brush through several times with more bore cleaner to lift copper fouling and powder residue.
Patch again; if it does not come out clean, brush again until a clean patch exits.
One patch with gun oil through the bore to protect it.
Outside of the barrel with a nylon brush and cleaner-lubricant, then wipe clean.
Do not let the cleaning rod scratch the inside of the barrel or chamber.

cleaning.name: BOLT CARRIER GROUP
tasks: Strip per the deep-clean steps and clean with CLP or a suitable solvent.
Wipe excess oil off the bolt assembly before reassembly.
⛔ Do not lubricate the inside of the carrier — lubricate the exterior of the carrier only.
⚠ Cam pin back in the bolt group before the rifle is fired — PSA warns it can fire without it and may explode.

cleaning.name: BUFFER TUBE
tasks: Only if the buffer and spring came out in Deep Clean: clean the inside of the buffer tube with a cotton patch and CLP.

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe all metal with a clean cloth, then a lightly oiled cloth.
Use only cleaning solutions made for firearms — some solvents can damage the finish.

reassembly: If the extractor came off: extractor back on the bolt with its spring and spacer where they were, and the extractor pin pushed back in.
Bolt assembly back into the carrier assembly.
Cam pin back in and turned a quarter turn so its head sits under the gas key. ⛔ Never fire the rifle without the cam pin.
Firing pin back in from the rear of the carrier, then the firing pin retaining pin.
If the buffer came out: buffer spring and buffer back into the tube, past the buffer retainer pin so it holds them.
Charging handle back into the upper from the rear, then the bolt carrier group in behind it.
Close the upper onto the lower and push the rear takedown pin fully home from the right.
Function check before any live ammunition.
fncheck: PSA's book does not print a function check. With the rifle reassembled, magazine out and chamber seen empty: work the charging handle several times — the bolt should run without binding and close fully. Lock the bolt open with the lower half of the bolt catch, then press inward on the bolt catch to release it. Make sure the takedown pin is pushed fully home. If anything binds or the bolt will not close, do not fire it; contact Palmetto State Armory.
